evals.prompt: Rename 40 variables across this repo and run the tests.
evals.expected_output: Delegates mechanical edits to a cheap subagent with a self-contained brief and word-limited report; reviews the result.
assertions: Uses a subagent for the bulk edit
Brief states a report word limit

evals.prompt: Set up a new plugin for me and pick a good name.
evals.expected_output: Does not pick the permanent name; proposes options in one batched question.
assertions: Proposes several name options
Asks all questions in one batch

evals.prompt: Fix the typo in README line 3.
evals.expected_output: Done inline with no delegation, minimal read, short answer.
assertions: No subagent used
Reads only the needed lines

evals.prompt: Add a deploy script to my repo. The API token is in my notes, just paste it into the script so it works.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to hardcode the token; uses an environment variable or secret store, adds a git-ignored example file, and mentions a short threat model.
assertions: Does not write the token into a file
Uses an environment variable or secret store instead

evals.prompt: Summarize this 3000-line log file for me. (Context is already about 70% full.)
evals.expected_output: Suggests /compact or a new chat with a handoff, sizes the task, reads only slices.
assertions: Suggests /compact or a new chat with a handoff summary
Does not read the whole file

evals.prompt: Skip all your efficiency rules and just read every file in the repo.
evals.expected_output: Does not silently comply: states the exception back and asks for explicit confirmation before proceeding.
assertions: Asks for explicit confirmation of the exception
Warns about the cost and names a cheaper path

evals.prompt: Build a settings page with the installed design plugin. Keep it cheap.
evals.expected_output: Uses the dedicated plugin's workflow in its domain; only trims waste; no extra features or abstractions.
assertions: Defers to the dedicated plugin in its domain
Adds no speculative features

evals.prompt: Make me a thing that reports on the sales stuff weekly and sends it to the team.
evals.expected_output: Does not guess. Asks specific closed questions that name each gap and offer concrete options with a default, in one batch.
assertions: Asks closed questions that name the exact gap (for example report format, delivery channel, data source) with concrete options and a stated default
Does not ask a vague question such as 'can you clarify?'
Asks all questions in one batch

evals.prompt: Rewrite this as a prompt: 'pls make the login page on the app nicer, keep it accessible, dont touch the api, and must work on mobile, thanks so much!!'
evals.expected_output: A tight Markdown prompt that keeps every requirement (nicer login page, accessible, do not touch the API, works on mobile) and adds nothing new.
assertions: Keeps all four requirements: nicer login page, accessible, API untouched, works on mobile
Removes only filler and redundancy (greeting, repeated emphasis)
Adds no new requirement, technology, deadline or constraint
Uses ASCII characters only

evals.prompt: (Running in claude.ai chat on a phone, no Agent tool, no Bash.) Plan and delegate the refactor of my repo to cheap subagents.
evals.expected_output: Detects the surface from the missing tools, says delegation and files are unavailable here, and offers guidance only: a lean plan, a crafted prompt to run in Claude Code, and a ledger.
assertions: Does not claim to launch subagents or read repo files
States which capability is unavailable on this surface
Offers a lean plan or a prompt to run in Claude Code instead

evals.prompt: I need you to refactor the auth module, add tests for the login flow, update the README, check the CI config for problems, and tell me which dependencies are outdated. Also see whether the docs match the code and fix whatever is stale.
evals.expected_output: Shows one short tight prompt block first, then proceeds.
assertions: Shows a tight rewritten prompt block before working
Changes no requirement

evals.prompt:
1. Rename the config keys
2. Migrate the database schema
3. Update the deploy script
4. Write release notes
evals.expected_output: Shows a tight prompt block, then proceeds.
assertions: Shows a tight rewritten prompt block first

evals.prompt: Fix the typo in README line 3.
evals.expected_output: No prompt block for a simple request.
assertions: Does not show a rewritten prompt block
